g.text: SIGN FLIP: actual target increases with arm ordinal, predictions decrease

text.style: font-style: italic; font-size: 7px; font-family: 'Liberation Sans', 'Arimo', 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #555555

g.text: What this shows: The actual BMD change correlates positively with arm ordinal (Spearman +0.367, p=0.023) — CONTROL loses more, EXERCISE loses less. But the model predictions correlate NEGATIVELY with arm ordinal (Spearman -0.356, p=0.028). If the model were simply detecting arm membership, we would expect predictions to track arm in the SAME direction as the target. The sign flip argues against pure arm detection.

text.style: font-style: italic; font-size: 7px; font-family: 'Liberation Sans', 'Arimo', 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #555555

g.text: What it does not show: Whether the sign flip is real signal (Reading A) or an artifact of 10×5 CV at n=38. These are EXPLORATORY correlations from 10×5 OOF predictions, NOT the LOOCV predictions behind the headline p=0.007. The LOOCV per-subject predictions were computed and discarded.

text.style: font-style: italic; font-size: 7px; font-family: 'Liberation Sans', 'Arimo', 'DejaVu Sans'; fill: #555555
